races.name: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up type for W H Harrison who has shown ability on Standard AW (place at this course on last visit) and comes here fresh off a 10-day turnaround; six-run form string includes a second at Goodwood but consistency is elusive, and at OR 54 this is comfortably within reach if Keenan can find a gap late.
runners_data.comment: Sands Of Seve caught the eye when runner-up two starts back and returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround with distance and going experience firmly in his favour at stall four carrying 135 lb; the concern is that sixth last time out suggests he needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Runamara
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher rides for the in-form John & Rhys Flint yard (3 from 10 over 14 days), and this hold-up type has a single AW placed run from four attempts on Standard — the 30-day break is not alarming but career form shows she fires occasionally rather than consistently, making her one to respect rather than anchor a race around.
runners_data.comment: Runamara has experience over today's trip and going, and returns after a 30-day break with our rating of 63 putting him top of the eight — though winless in his last six starts, a second five starts back hints at ability worth respecting off a mark of 53.

runners_data.name: Tommie's Angel
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies runner with only three career starts and the longest break in the field at 61 days; although this is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, the limited form over 6–7f on softer ground than today suggests trip and surface doubts, and the redistribution to midfield simply reflects how crowded the rear of this field is — watch for a debut on this configuration.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — unplaced most recently, seventh two starts back, and a fourth three starts back — Tommie's Angel returns after 61 days off, carries 133 lb from stall seven, and, ranked seventh of eight on our figures, faces a stiff ask here despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: Carries the most compelling recent form in the field — a hat-trick of placed efforts at this exact course and distance on Standard AW, most recently a win — and Tom Kiely-Marshall comes in on a 7-day turnaround; despite being a true hold-up type mapped mid-pack due to field congestion, the in-form AW profile here is the one others need to match.
runners_data.comment: Havin A Flyer arrives in career-best form — a winner last time out, and placed in three of her four starts before that — carrying 133 lb from stall 2 on familiar distance and going; the weight burden is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: A Lott Of Kane
runners_data.note: Joey Haynes takes the mount on a horse with a win and a second from its most recent Standard AW appearances at this trip — 52 days off is a minor concern but the form cycle is pointing back toward the track; Chelsea Banham's yard is quiet (0 from 4 in 14 days), and this is a natural closer operating in a field where every rival shares the same profile, making position at the furlong pole critical.
runners_data.comment: A Lott Of Kane boasts a win three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating of 56 suggesting he holds strong claims from stall 6; the concern is 52 days off the track since his last outing.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave, a jockey with strong Wolverhampton AW experience, partners this hold-up type just seven days after its last run — back-to-back seconds on Standard AW (including at Wolverhampton) set the scene well; Adam Kirby's yard is cold (0 from 10 in 14 days), which tempers enthusiasm, but the horse's fitness and Cosgrave's course craft make it a realistic threat if it settles well and travels into the sprint.
runners_data.comment: My Mate Mackley has been consistently placed in recent starts — second last time out, second two starts back, and third three starts back — yet his sole win in this sequence came four starts back, and he's drawn stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Viennetta
runners_data.note: William Carson and Michael Blake team up with a filly that has only run three times, all on Firsby or Goodwood and never on AW Standard — the 59-day absence combined with an untested surface profile makes this largely unknown, and while the hold-up position is natural, her current form string (57-0) does not inspire confidence ahead of more experienced rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Viennetta returns after 59 days off with little recent form to recommend her; she has run over today's trip before, and stall three is her lot at 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Princess Of Limnos
runners_data.note: De Sousa's booking elevates a filly who has run twice on this course (including a third at Firby but two poor efforts at Wolverhampton on Standard), and the ⚠ fade flag is significant — 79 days off is the longest absence in the field, and Tony Carroll's yard is active (5 from 34 over 14 days) which may signal a readiness angle, but the finishing tendency and course record limit expectations materially.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the bright spot for Princess Of Limnos, though she was ninth two starts back and winless in her last three, with 79 days between runs adding a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and carries 126 lb from stall 8.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of eight runners with no confirmed front-runner, meaning no horse is likely to impose a natural gallop and the race will almost certainly be decided by a late dash from the pack. Every single runner in this field carries a hold-up profile, creating an unusual scenario where the entire field defaults to waiting tactics — the result will be a compressed, sprint-finish affair with horses fanning wide in the closing furlong. With Standard Wolverhampton AW conditions offering a fair surface, closing ability and a turn of foot in the final 100 yards will be the decisive factor rather than tactical positioning. The field holds far more genuine hold-up types than can be cleanly separated on the pace map — Tommie's Angel, A Lott Of Kane, My Mate Mackley, Havin A Flyer, Viennetta, and Princess Of Limnos are all redistributed runners, and none is likely to take up a materially different position from the others, meaning Sands Of Seve and Runamara are likely to be the most prominent horses by default simply through being the least inclined to wait. This race shape favours the horse with the sharpest turn of foot and best recent form on Standard AW, as there will be no pace to chase down and the winner must manufacture their own momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Best Closer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches throughout and the race is decided by a sharp final-furlong kick with no horse gaining a meaningful positional advantage.
scenarios.body: The entire field races in a tight group with no pace injection, producing a wall-to-wall sprint from the 2f pole as jockeys ask simultaneously; the horse with the sharpest acceleration and best recent AW form on Standard ground takes it. Havin A Flyer's six consecutive placed or winning runs on Standard AW, including three straight places at this course and distance, gives it the profile to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Delivers Position
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses from a favourable draw (high draws at Wolverhampton 5f carry a rail advantage) secure a slender positional edge and dictate the tempo of the sprint.
scenarios.body: A horse gaining a few lengths advantage off the break — even marginally — can control the sprint against this field of pure hold-up types who will not challenge early for position. My Mate Mackley's recent back-to-back placed efforts on Standard AW and Wolverhampton experience make it the likeliest beneficiary if it secures a clean break from a clean draw.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Form Hotpot Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate throughout and a single horse produces one clear late burst of acceleration while others cancel each other out.
scenarios.body: With every runner trying to close at the same moment, a horse carrying the strongest current form and most relevant Standard AW experience can thread through the gaps as rivals interfere with one another. A Lott Of Kane, winner and runner-up on recent Standard AW appearances at this trip, is the natural profile for this scenario given its course-going fitness.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Underdogs Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If a fully rested or lightly raced runner who has benefited from an extended break returns sharper and produces a career-best effort against a competitively weak field.
scenarios.body: Horses returning from breaks of 52–79 days — Tommie's Angel, A Lott Of Kane, Viennetta, Princess Of Limnos — carry unknown readiness but equally face a weaker OR band that might expose their potential if they return to form. Princess Of Limnos, with De Sousa booked and a run on the board at this course, is the wildcard to consider, though her finishing tendencies on Standard ground remain a concern.

watchPoints.text: Havin A Flyer has the strongest course-and-distance profile in the field — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) can find daylight in a compressed finish, as this horse's turn of foot on Standard AW has been consistently demonstrated.

My Mate Mackley and A Lott Of Kane share almost identical recent AW form profiles and will likely be tracking each other in the closing stages — if they meet trouble in running simultaneously, both could be denied in a finish that may be decided by inches.

Princess Of Limnos is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — with De Sousa aboard and a 79-day break, monitor her early in the betting to see if market confidence supports the fitness angle, because the form without that support is thin.

With every horse in this field carrying a hold-up profile, draw positions at Wolverhampton 5f (where high draws are traditionally favoured on the AW circuit) should be checked once stalls are announced — a significant positional edge could be granted to whoever draws widest on a track that bends right-handed throughout.

Viennetta has never raced on AW Standard and steps down from 6f — William Carson's ability to settle a young filly on debut at this course and surface configuration is worth monitoring, particularly if she breaks well and ends up in an unfamiliar position ahead of her natural hold-up tendencies.

runners_data.name: Connie Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a 169-day absence and a visor fitment to sharpen focus; her five recent runs show sim-going figures of 5/9 with no wins or placed efforts on Standard AW, making this trip and surface a significant ask on return.
runners_data.comment:

runners_data.name: Cephalus
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type warned for fading in finishes, and ten runs on this exact surface at 8f show only one win and two placings in fifteen; stepping up markedly in trip is a leap of faith, though a recent 23-day turnaround keeps fitness intact.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Cephalus nonetheless heads this field on our rating and has run over today's trip, with 23 days since his last outing leaving him fresh enough to strike — though his recent form figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: The Dark Baron
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 7f at Standard going 17 days ago and has two wins plus seven placed runs in fifteen similar-going outings; the 3lb claim from Coughlan is a meaningful allowance and his style of racing close to pace suits this uncontested lead scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Just the one win in his last five starts with a sequence of fourths and a sixth making him hard to fancy ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, though he does bring distance experience and a quick 17-day turnaround suggests he's fit.

runners_data.name: Between Me And U
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f Standard, but this horse is a genuine hold-up type compressed into a midfield slot because of the overcrowded rear; at 22 days since that win the fitness is solid, and the tongue-tie has been a consistent companion, but position in running will likely compromise its chance.
runners_data.comment: Between Me And U arrives on the back of a recent win and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat from stall two carrying 134 lb; the concern is whether he can reproduce that form after a string of disappointing efforts before it.

runners_data.name: Tilani
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who has won twice at 8f on Good but has no AW Standard form at all; Morris is experienced enough to manage the fractions, yet the style-fit flag highlights a modest AW record and the step to 1m½f is entirely unexplored — the front is his but the unknown surface remains the key caveat.
runners_data.comment: Tilani has experience over today's trip and returns after 27 days off, but his last two runs read 8th and 2nd, suggesting inconsistency; the encouraging news is back-to-back wins three and four starts back, though he needs to rediscover that form from stall 12 off 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Volto di Medusa
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won over 8f at Standard 22 days ago and wears a hood; sim-going figures of 11/15 with two wins and four placings show he can find the frame here, but the structural overcrowding at the rear means getting a clear run is the barrier rather than ability.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win three starts back but has struggled either side of that, finishing unplaced or well held in his other recent runs; has experience of today's trip and going, though inconsistency is the clear concern from draw 9 off 136 lb.

runners_data.name: King Chaos
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from a 191-day absence, but he won over 12f at this track on Standard going and the extra trip here is squarely in his comfort zone; a record of one win and three placings in nine similar-going runs suggests he handles these conditions and is optimally positioned to sit second or third behind Tilani.
runners_data.comment: King Chaos won two starts back but hasn't been seen for 191 days, and that lengthy absence is the obvious query; he has run over today's trip and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Portman Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has run seven times on Standard AW without a win, recording only two placings; a 7-day turnaround is brisk and the consistent mid-to-rear positioning in all recent starts leaves him exposed in a shape that does not produce late closers easily.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of sixths most recently, Portman Blue has run over today's trip and steps back up quickly on just seven days' rest — a rating of 67 offers marginal encouragement, though he has work to do from seventh in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Bun Bang Fai
runners_data.note: Long-absentee returning after 301 days and a true hold-up horse displaced into a midfield mapping; with no win or placed effort in six Standard-going runs and a blank sim-going record here, the layoff combined with positional compromise makes this a very difficult starting point.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and off the track for 301 days, Bun Bang Fai faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 132 lb, and a ranking of 12th of 13 on our figures leaves little to cling to — experience over today's trip is the one crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Pearly Squirrel
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with five placed efforts in fifteen similar-going runs and the class of De Sousa engaged, but like several others she cannot achieve her natural rear position in this race shape; the 20-day turnaround is fine and the consistent top-five finishes are genuine, yet the redistribution limits her expected winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Pearly Squirrel arrives here fourth last time out but with a third two starts back, and her consistent presence in the frame — three placings in her last six starts — marks her out as a genuine threat; the main worry is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Cy Twombly
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with eight runs on Standard AW and not a single win or placing; a visor is worn to try to sharpen the response but the profile of finishing in the back half of the field is persistent, and being pushed further from the rear than natural compounds the problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three finishes of ninth or worse in that sequence, Cy Twombly is hard to fancy here; he has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround, but his recent figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: R P McMurphy
runners_data.note: Has won twice and placed seven times in twelve Standard-going runs making this one of the better hold-up profiles in the field, and Stott is a shrewd AW operator; the redistribution into midfield hurts, but the consistent proximity to the placed positions on this surface gives it a residual each-way case if the field fans wide.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying 130 lb from stall 8, R P McMurphy heads into this on the back of two poor efforts — unplaced last time out and eighth the run before — making him hard to fancy, despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Onslow Gardens
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with zero wins and two placings in fifteen similar-going runs and a 46-day absence; Clutterbuck is a conditional rider and the combination of true hold-up style being raced out of position, modest form on this surface, and a less experienced pilot makes this one of the weaker propositions in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Onslow Gardens did show a flash of ability with a third three runs back, though a seventh and ninth since suggest that form may flatter him; carrying 130 lb from stall seven, the 46-day break adds mild uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Tilani is the lone confirmed front runner in this 13-runner 1m½f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to press hard from the off, Luke Morris should be able to dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from gate to straight on Standard Wolverhampton AW. The Prominent types — The Dark Baron and King Chaos — will track behind but neither has the profile or the intent to go with Tilani hard early, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than frantic, preserving the leader's stamina. That controlled tempo on a flat, right-handed circuit strongly favours horses sitting close to the pace in second or third who can maintain momentum into the straight, rather than those coming from deep who need a true test to close the gap. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Between Me And U, Pearly Squirrel, Bun Bang Fai, Cy Twombly, R P McMurphy and Onslow Gardens are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and in reality only the first two of those are likely to find positions anywhere near their natural ground — the rest will find themselves bunched and unable to produce the wide run they need. Tactical verdict: prominent and close-tracking profiles are best placed in this shape; hold-up horses face a significant structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tilani Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Tilani is allowed to control the fractions unchallenged and Morris manages the tempo intelligently throughout.
scenarios.body: Tilani has form figures of 1-1 on Good ground but steps onto AW Standard for the first time; the uncontested lead on a flat track with no one pressing means energy is conserved for the straight, and a horse with recent win form at 8f has the tactical edge in this shape. The Prominent types immediately behind benefit most as passengers in a steady pace-train, with The Dark Baron and King Chaos ideally poised to pounce if Tilani ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tilani's inexperience on AW or the slightly longer 1m½f trip causes the lead to be relinquished turning for home.
scenarios.body: The Dark Baron has been placed nine times in fifteen similar-going runs and Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim makes the weight attractive, while King Chaos won over 12f at this track in this going and handles the trip well. If Tilani fades in the final furlong, these two are optimally placed to inherit the race without needing a sustained late burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and a horse pushed into midfield manages to find a clear run turning in.
scenarios.body: Between Me And U won last time over 8f at Standard going and, if permitted to travel wide and produce its natural late effort, could benefit from a bunched finish where positional accidents create gaps. Pearly Squirrel has five placed efforts in fifteen similar-going runs and Silvestre De Sousa is capable of threading through a tightly packed field, making this the most plausible of the hold-up scenarios despite the structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Late Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight, causing leaders to tighten up and creating a late sprint that suits deep-closers.
scenarios.body: R P McMurphy has two wins and seven placed efforts in twelve Standard-going runs and Kevin Stott is an experienced handler of AW routes, giving it an outside chance if traffic clears late. Volto di Medusa won over 8f at Standard and has AW form, but with both horses carrying the full redistribution penalty this is a low-probability outcome requiring multiple things to go wrong ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Tilani (Morris) will go straight to the front — watch whether he is pressed for the lead at any point in the first three furlongs, because an uncontested lead makes this horse considerably more dangerous than if King Chaos or The Dark Baron move up to challenge early.

Between Me And U is a genuine hold-up horse crammed into midfield by the weight of traffic at the rear — watch whether Keenan elects to drop it back to its natural position instead, which would signal it is being ridden for its true style and could emerge as a late dark-horse threat if the field strings out.

Bun Bang Fai's 301-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a significant margin — watch the market moves and paddock behaviour closely, as a cold-horse debutant returning from nearly a year off is an unpredictable element in a pace-sensitive race shape.

King Chaos returns from 191 days off but previously won at this exact track and distance combination on Standard going — watch how quickly Kaiya Fraser positions him behind Tilani, because a smooth stalking move from second or third could make the layoff irrelevant if he is spot-on.

The Dark Baron carries the benefit of a recent win 17 days ago and Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim — watch whether the claim shunts him into contention at a weight that makes him one of the better-handicapped runners in the race on adjusted ratings.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Location Location
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at Goodwood and here on Standard, suits a pressured pace from a prominent berth; simple headgear, trainer Fanshawe in solid 14-day form at 3/19, and the 29-day absence is not a concern given recent fitness — keep safe on a track where her style fits.

runners_data.name: Ongombo
runners_data.note: High official rating of 120 is conspicuous in this restricted band but both career starts ended in defeat on this exact surface and trip; hold-up style requires a stronger pace than usual to generate a meaningful run, and trainer Fellowes has modest recent figures.

runners_data.name: Zohar
runners_data.note: Flags a fading pattern in the finishing stages and has failed to place in three starts including two on Standard going; the hold-up style compounds the issue here with two leaders ensuring the race won't be run to suit a horse that already struggles to sustain its effort.

runners_data.name: Conscientious
runners_data.note: First-time starter for Archie Watson, whose stable is running at 1/13 over 14 days — not a barn firing on all cylinders right now — but lightly-raced debutants with unknown style profiles always carry an element of surprise in fields like this; watch market moves late.

runners_data.name: God Of Titans
runners_data.note: Sole start produced a distant 17th of 17 at Goodwood on Good ground; fading-in-finish flag is a real concern and the hold-up profile in a front-runner-dominated race makes a big improvement hard to see — Clare Hobson's stable is cold at 0/3 in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Montgomery Bell
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Heather Main, whose stable has produced 0 winners from 8 runners in the past fortnight; style is entirely unknown which adds uncertainty, though the field's openness means he cannot be entirely dismissed if well-schooled at home.

runners_data.name: Postremo
runners_data.note: Ran sixth over 5f on Good ground 87 days ago, stepping up to 6f here after a long absence; the unknown-style tag and lengthy gap since racing make it hard to assess, though J S Moore's yard has two winners from 12 runners lately suggesting reasonable fitness.

runners_data.name: Supreme Star
runners_data.note: The chief pace-setter and one of two confirmed front-runners in this race; his second over this 6f course suggests he handles the track, but the threat of Ouragan likely forcing a contested duel is the key risk to his chances — Botti's yard is firing at 3/13 in the 14-day period.

runners_data.name: Angel Sense
runners_data.note: Strong placed profile on Standard going with two placed efforts from four tries on this surface; prominent style from a tracking position with De Sousa aboard gives her a clear tactical edge in a contested-pace scenario — the tongue-tie headgear is noted and she looks a key player.

runners_data.name: Huda's Joy
runners_data.note: Another debutant with no public form and an unknown style; Jamie Osborne's yard is operating at 3/12 recently which is encouraging, and first-timers from that operation have won maidens before — the market on the day will be the clearest guide to expectations.

runners_data.name: Ouragan
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner who will contest the early lead with Supreme Star; his second on Good and fifth on Standard show ability, but the energy cost of fighting for position from the gate in a 6f sprint could leave him vulnerable late — Archie Watson's overall 14-day figures are modest.

runners_data.name: Trust In Far
runners_data.note: Ran just 6 days ago and has a string of poor finishes including 9th, 11th and 7th in recent outings; the hold-up style on a track where the pace is set to be strong gives little hope, and the very quick turnaround is a concern unless the trainer has a specific reason for targeting this.

races.paceDynamic: Supreme Star and Ouragan are both confirmed front-runners over this 6f Wolverhampton AW straight, and with neither likely to concede the lead willingly, the early exchanges will be genuinely contested rather than a controlled solo show. That rivalry should produce an honest, pressured gallop from the off, burning through both horses' reserves before the final furlong begins to bite. Angel Sense and Location Location, sitting prominently just off the speed, are ideally positioned to exploit any late weakening from the leaders without having to make their own energy expenditure too early. This race shape — a genuinely run, competitive pace set by two leaders fighting each other — tilts the tactical advantage firmly toward prominent racers and close-tracking hold-up horses who can arrive late with something in reserve, rather than the leaders themselves who will have done the bulk of the work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme Star and Ouragan push each other hard enough to leave both vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The sustained battle up front drains both leaders before the line, opening the door for prominent-to-midfield horses to sweep past in the closing stages; Angel Sense, with her consistent placed form on this surface and strong Standard going record, is ideally suited to capitalise from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Supreme Star — establishes a clear break early and dictates an even, controlled tempo rather than a wasteful duel.
scenarios.body: A settled lead from Supreme Star would allow him to conserve energy and simply gallop rivals into the ground on a track where leaders with class can still win; his recent second over this course and distance gives him a genuine each-way profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Outclass Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced or debut runners — Conscientious, Montgomery Bell, or Huda's Joy — arrives with significantly superior ability masked by limited form data.
scenarios.body: Maiden races at this level are routinely won by unexposed types whose homework has suggested above-average ability, and Archie Watson's Conscientious in particular carries the yard's strong recent strike rate into an open contest; a clean break and any tactical flexibility could see a debutant go clear in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Very Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly scorching and even prominent racers get swallowed up, leaving only deep hold-up horses with finishing runs.
scenarios.body: Ongombo and Zohar are mapped as hold-up types, though both carry fading-in-finish concerns and poor Standard-going records that make a late flourish hard to fully trust; this scenario requires near-perfect fractions and some trouble in running to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Supreme Star and Ouragan are both genuine front-runners and will almost certainly contest the early lead — watch which one has established a clear advantage by the 4f marker, as the one who blinks first may be beaten before the final furlong.

Angel Sense's tongue-tie and consistent placed form on Standard going make her the chief beneficiary if the pace duel unfolds as expected — if she tracks the leaders smoothly, she could hit the front late without being headed.

Conscientious, Montgomery Bell, and Huda's Joy are all first-time starters with unknown tactical profiles — any of them drifting significantly in the market pre-race would be a meaningful signal given the limited data available on their ability.

Zohar and God Of Titans both carry official fading-in-finish flags — in a race likely to be run at a strong early pace, their hold-up styles make them vulnerable to running out of race before their finishing effort materialises; treat both with significant caution.

Trust In Far returns after just 6 days and has shown little in four career starts; the quick reappearance is worth monitoring in case the trainer has spotted a drop in class, but the evidence on the clock and in the form book does not currently support optimism.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Claiming Stakes

runners_data.name: Buzz Box
runners_data.note: Consistent Wolverhampton specialist with three wins on this track over 5f on standard, stepping up to 6f which is a minor query, but prominent style suits a controlled solo pace perfectly and Darragh Keenan's local course knowledge is an asset.
runners_data.comment: Buzz Box showed his class with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and returns here fit on 25 days' rest with experience over today's trip — the concern is that his last two runs have yielded a fourth and a ninth, raising questions about current form.

runners_data.name: Jungle Drums
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a recent win over this C&D in standard conditions; trainer Jamie Osborne in solid T14 form (3/12), but needs the pace to be genuine to get competitive from off the speed and soft-ground form can be set aside here.
runners_data.comment: Jungle Drums catches the eye on the back of a win last time out, with a further success five starts back adding recent substance to his form. He has run over today's trip before, and at 16 days fresh, conditions look to suit this 142 lb carrier from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Trust Sergei
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose real position is further back than the map depicts — three redistribution horses crowd the rear, pushing him into midfield — but his recent run of 3-1-2 in form is compelling and Gary Hanmer sends him here with the style mismatch the key caveat.
runners_data.comment: Trust Sergei arrives in decent nick at 20 days between runs, has run over today's trip, and showed a win two starts back, but ranked last of 11 on our figures he faces a stiff ask, and that lofty 139 lb burden makes life even harder to fancy.

runners_data.name: Havanagreattime
runners_data.note: 328 days off is an enormous concern and Ruth Carr's T14 return rate (4/22) does not inspire confidence for a horse returning cold; hold-up style needs pace to work with, and the combination of ring rustiness and a tactical disadvantage makes this a speculative runner at best.
runners_data.comment: Havanagreattime brings strong credentials on paper — our rating puts him clear of these rivals — but he's winless in recent starts and a return from 328 days off is the obvious question mark against a horse who has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Hockney
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe winless in the last 14 days (0/8) but this horse has won over 6f standard and 6f soft, tracks pace well from a prominent position, and William Cox has the ability to slot in just behind the leader if Hunky Dory goes forward smoothly.
runners_data.comment: Hockney won two starts back but has been well beaten either side of that success, and 49 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and carries 134 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Manly Fireball
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with solid placed form over this C&D (5th and 1st and 2nd from recent 6f standard runs), prominent style fits the expected race shape naturally, and the 7lb claimer Donagh Murphy needs to hold his position in a field with several horses who want to be prominent.
runners_data.comment: Manly Fireball showed he can win at this level with a victory two starts back, though a fifth last time out tempers that form, and our rating of 74 suggests he may have more to do against the principals from stall two at 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Hunky Dory
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner here — the key pace-setter for this race shape — but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) notes he is nudged slightly out of his optimal role, and 71 days off plus a headgear absence may blunt the expected front-running dominance; Kevin Stott is an able partner to manage a solo lead.
runners_data.comment: Hunky Dory landed a winner three starts back and has run over today's trip, giving him solid claims here off 128 lb from stall 11; the main concern is that his last two efforts have been modest and he returns after 71 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Mission Command
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie/visor) worn, but distance concern is real — all recent wins or places at 6-8f on softer ground, and course form shows nothing competitive at Wolverhampton; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a minor plus for a horse that needs much more pace than this race is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Mission Command won three starts back but has since posted back-to-back sevenths, suggesting he's hit a flat patch; he has run over today's trip and returns after 19 days, though those recent finishes make him hard to fancy at present.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins on good ground are eye-catching, but the blinkered mare is a genuine front-runner squeezed into a midfield slot by the race shape — whether Alexandra Egan (7lb claim) can push her forward to her natural prominent position against Hunky Dory's established lead preference is the critical question.
runners_data.comment: Punchbowl Flyer's figures place him ninth of eleven, and it's hard to ignore the unplaced and bottom-half finishes deeper in his recent record. That said, he arrives off back-to-back wins, has run over today's trip, and draws stall four carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Hakin Adraar
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted three-year-old who last ran just 9 days ago and is a hold-up type placed into midfield by the distribution; blinkers on, but all recent form has come over 7-8f and dropping to 6f on a flat AW track is a compression the form profile doesn't fully support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fifth last time out the best he could manage in recent outings, Hakin Adraar ranks tenth of eleven on our figures and looks hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's trip and returns quickly after just nine days.

runners_data.name: Seu Jo
runners_data.note: Recorded a win over 8f standard and is a true hold-up horse shuffled forward in the map; at 3 years old over a sharp 6f with 50 days off, the combination of trip reduction, layoff and positional compromise gives Sean D Bowen a tough brief despite his undoubted ability to ride a waiting race.
runners_data.comment: Seu Jo landed a win four starts back but has been below par since, going unplaced in two of his last three; the 50-day absence is a query, though he has run over today's trip and carries a manageable 119 lb from stall five.

races.paceDynamic: Hunky Dory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f AW contest at Wolverhampton and, with no genuine rival to press him for the lead, he should be able to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop from the gates. Standard going at Wolverhampton typically rewards horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the turn into the straight, meaning Hunky Dory's lone lead should set a tempo that is workable rather than suicidal. Buzz Box and Hockney are the most likely prominent challengers to sit just off the pace and fire their challenges from just behind the leader, while the hold-up brigade — Jungle Drums, Havanagreattime, Trust Sergei and Mission Command — will be making ground from further back into a pace that may not fully stretch. The race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking profile who can travel handily without being involved in early scrimmaging; true hold-up horses face a stiff ask if the tempo is merely steady rather than searching. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Punchbowl Flyer, Seu Jo and Hakin Adraar are genuine prominent or hold-up horses pushed into midfield slots, with Punchbowl Flyer arguably most capable of muscling into a genuine prominent position if she breaks sharply.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hunky Dory Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Hunky Dory breaks cleanly, settles into a controlled lead and is never seriously challenged for position through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hunky Dory controls the pace from the front, setting a rhythm that suits close-tracking types while ensuring hold-up horses face a long run to get competitive; the prominent horses who can lock on and sustain their effort into the straight have the clearest path to the winner's enclosure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If Buzz Box and Hockney track Hunky Dory comfortably and have enough in reserve to nail him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace set by Hunky Dory proves just enough to soften him but not so extreme that a close tracker cannot sustain a challenge; Buzz Box's consistent Wolverhampton form and Hockney's ability to rattle home from just off the pace make both dangerous at the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Hunky Dory's uncontested lead produces a genuinely strong gallop that causes the race to truly string out and create late ground.
scenarios.body: Jungle Drums is the most believable beneficiary given his recent winning form and solid record over 6f on standard AW, though he needs the pace to be genuine rather than dawdling; Havanagreattime is a big question mark after 328 days off but has the profile to finish powerfully if conditions set up for a sweeping run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off A Strong Break
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early pace develops — most likely triggered by Punchbowl Flyer forcing to the front — and the complexion of the race changes sharply.
scenarios.body: Punchbowl Flyer is the most likely horse to disrupt Hunky Dory's expected solo lead, but racing out of her natural slot reduces her winning chance; a truly fast pace from the outset would theoretically open the door for the deepest closers, though the redistribution of several hold-up types into midfield slots makes this the least reliable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Buzz Box has three wins at Wolverhampton on standard and a prominent style that locks perfectly onto Hunky Dory's expected lead — watch for Darragh Keenan to track closely from the outset and challenge sharply from the 2f pole.

Punchbowl Flyer is a genuine prominent type who may challenge Hunky Dory for the front — if she breaks fast and forces an early duel, the entire pace scenario shifts from controlled to contested, opening the race up for hold-up horses.

Havanagreattime returns after 328 days off; if Ruth Carr has her spot-on she could be dangerous late, but a horse at this price with that layoff warrants monitoring in the market for any significant support that might signal stable confidence.

Mission Command has headgear listed (tv) and has shown he can win when conditions suit, but his best form has come at 7-8f and on softer surfaces — watch whether he travels with any fluency in the first half of the race as a guide to his effectiveness at 6f here.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Trust Sergei, Seu Jo and Hakin Adraar — are all racing partially out of their natural position; if any of them show unusual early speed in the first furlong it may indicate a change of tactics that could alter the back-half dynamics of the race.

races.name: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who will likely lead unchallenged; William Haggas yard in solid recent form (6/34 14-day), but she is officially rated for a prominent role and this maps her technically out of pure lead position — her best chance rests entirely on dictating terms cleanly from stall to line over a trip that stretches her current form profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Evening Fades does at least bring consistent placed-proximity form and is fitter for a run 19 days ago; carrying 135 lb looks a tough ask, however, for a filly rated 60 hunting improvement.

runners_data.name: African Gib
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's hold-up performer returns after 59 days off and has no wins from four tries on Standard surfaces; Robert Havlin takes the ride but the absence and zero AW wins are concerns for a horse that needs cover and a strong pace to produce its best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, African Gib has struggled for consistency and returns after 59 days off carrying 135 lb — a stiff ask. Connections will need a significant upturn in form.

runners_data.name: Goldfinder
runners_data.note: Consistent type with a useful second last time on Standard over this exact 12f trip, going five-for-five on AW Standard going overall; William Cox rides for a yard with one winner from five recent runners, and the step back to 1m4f from 1m6f should suit his profile well.
runners_data.comment: Goldfinder shaped well when runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 68 putting him narrowly top of these on adjusted figures. Winless in his last five starts, but that second is an encouraging springboard after 58 days off.

runners_data.name: Worlington
runners_data.note: Landed a 1m4f Good win recently and boasts solid second-place efforts at this trip; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a plus, tongue-tie fitted, and a horse with five runs on Standard going for one win shows his best on a surface he handles — course form and recent upswing make him interesting.
runners_data.comment: Worlington landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, with 24 days between runs suggesting he returns fresh and ready; the main concern is a disappointing ninth last time out that he'll need to put firmly behind him.

runners_data.name: Forever Perfect
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies-trained mare with a strong record at this trip on Standard, including a win over 1m4f here; one win and four places from six runs at today's distance/surface combination is the best statistical profile in the field, and Kaiya Fraser rides a horse that clearly belongs at this level.
runners_data.comment: Forever Perfect shaped with consistent placed form, finishing second two starts back and third last time out, and has run over today's trip — but connections will need her to return as sharp after 55 days off.

runners_data.name: La Kosmos
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for Alan King but the yard is 0/8 in the last 14 days and the horse has no wins from four Standard starts; the step up to 1m4f from shorter trips could be interesting but the form string of 64-78 does not encourage confidence at current level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with an eighth last time out and a seventh two starts back, La Kosmos heads here 59 days fresh and carrying 135 lb — she has run over today's trip, but little else in her recent profile invites confidence.

runners_data.name: Baron Wagstaff
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose natural race shape involves sitting last and waiting for gaps — Jonny Peate will find himself in a midfield slot he wouldn't typically choose because of the volume of closers in this field; three finishes outside the top four from four recent runs and no wins from two Standard starts make him difficult to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a string of mid-division finishes offering little encouragement, Baron Wagstaff faces a stiff ask here; he does come into this fresh enough at 28 days since his last run, but ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, he is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Crown Inn To Win
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the mount on a horse with a striking record over this trip on Standard — one win and four places from eight attempts — but 82 days off the track and hood fitted are the key questions; a natural hold-up horse pushed closer to midfield by the field's composition, yet the form profile here is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Placed in five of his last six starts — third last time out and a winner the start before — Crown Inn To Win has experience over today's trip, but 82 days off the track is a concern, and 133 lb is no gimme at an official mark of 58.

runners_data.name: Sir Griflet
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's gelding ran only five days ago and carries a tongue-tie; a hold-up horse by nature, the congested rear means Stevie Donohoe will be tracking mid-pack rather than sitting last, and a form string showing no wins from seven Standard outings with a latest effort of 0 (pulled up or refused) is a significant deterrent.
runners_data.comment: Sir Griflet has been largely consistent without threatening, posting a fourth three starts back, and our rating of 65 puts him ahead of his official mark — a strong case for progress. The main risk is his unplaced return five days ago, leaving fitness questions after a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Si White
runners_data.note: Won over 11f on Standard most recently for Sir Mark Prescott, who is in sizzling 14-day form (9/22); a hold-up horse by inclination who finds himself mapped into a midfield slot given the field's composition, and the step up to 1m4f from his last winning trip is the key question — Luke Morris knows the yard's runners well.
runners_data.comment: Sharp enough to win last time out — a winner seven days ago — but his overall profile in recent starts shows consistency has been elusive, with a sixth two starts back. He has run over today's trip and carries 133 lb off an official mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick send out this hold-up type on a quick 16-day turnaround; three finishes of 5th-6th-6th from four AW Standard runs and a best effort of fifth suggest consistent mediocrity rather than a lurking talent, and Lewis Edmunds has limited options from the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of mid-pack finishes, Blue Tulip is hard to fancy here — ranked last on our figures and carrying 129 lb. She does have experience over today's trip, but that's about as much as can be said in her favour.

runners_data.name: Rajbello
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's hold-up performer returns after 55 days and has a form string of 5-8-5-5 on Standard, all without troubling the judge; Alexandra Egan claims 7lbs which helps with the weight, but the horse has never won over 12f on this surface and the pattern of mid-division finishes does not suggest the trip or pace scenario here will unlock anything new.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and not seen out for 55 days, Rajbello returns here with fitness to prove; he has run over today's trip before and our rating suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 53 implies, though consistency remains the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Evening Fades is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to challenge for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested pace over Wolverhampton's 1m4f Polytrack circuit. Behind her, the race is stacked with hold-up types — Forever Perfect, Crown Inn To Win, Worlington, African Gib, La Kosmos, Goldfinder, and several redistributed horses — meaning the midfield and rear will be densely populated, creating a tactical vacuum between Evening Fades and the chasing pack. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can absorb at the rear: Sir Griflet, Crown Inn To Win, Baron Wagstaff, Si White, Blue Tulip and Rajbello are all true hold-up types forced into midfield positions they would not naturally seek. With Evening Fades able to dictate a sustainable gallop on the front end, this race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel prominently close to the pace or pick up efficiently from just off it — pure deep closers will find the tempo insufficient to generate the late run they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fades Leads, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades dictates a fair but controlled gallop and is not reeled in until the home straight.
scenarios.body: Evening Fades sets an uncontested pace, the field strings out behind her, and horses who have been tracking within three lengths of her at the turn are best placed to collar her late; a soft lead can become a winning lead over this trip on a flat AW circuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to set up a strong finishing challenge for horses sitting second to fourth throughout.
scenarios.body: A well-judged hold on Evening Fades at a close range allows a prominent tracker to sweep past in the final furlong as the leader ties up; this suits horses with tactical speed and strong AW form at the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades sets a genuinely strong early tempo that blows the field apart and leaves space for a late finisher to thread through.
scenarios.body: A hot pace causes early carnage in the tightly bunched midfield and a horse with a powerful finishing kick gets a clear run from the back; however, most of the nominal hold-up types here are redistributed and not naturally suited to this role, which suppresses this scenario's likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades misses the break or is taken on early, producing a falsely slow race that ends in a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: A crawl-then-sprint scenario turns this into a sprint for the line from a tightly grouped pack, wiping out the hold-up horses who need a true test; horses with tactical versatility and a turn of foot become the dangers.

watchPoints.text: Evening Fades — watch whether she breaks cleanly and establishes the lead without incident; if she misses the break or is bustled for position early, the entire race shape collapses and no single horse takes control of the pace.

Crown Inn To Win — an 82-day absence combined with hood fitting means Silvestre De Sousa may need an educational run before she hits peak form; if fresh and sharp she is dangerously well-suited to this trip and surface, but the fitness question is real.

Si White — Sir Mark Prescott's runners for Luke Morris often improve sharply on quick returns, and the 9/22 14-day trainer strike rate demands respect; watch whether the step up to 1m4f from his winning 11f trip is within his comfort zone in the market.

Worlington — tongue-tie fitted for the first time alongside a recent course win over this trip signals a trainer intent on maximising this horse today; if the headgear produces a more focused effort, his profile of placed runs at this trip becomes very relevant.

The midfield cluster — with six or more horses all forced to race closer than their natural position, watch for crowding and interference around the home turn as horses who want to be at the rear find themselves bunched in the middle; a clean passage to the outside rail in the straight could prove decisive.

runners_data.name: Dashing Donkey
runners_data.note: Has shown placed form at 7f Standard (2 places from 7 sim-going runs) but is a natural hold-up horse who will be racing in a more advanced position than ideal given rear-field congestion; William Stone trainer angle offers little edge and the style compromise tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Faster Bee
runners_data.note: Course-specialist with 2 wins at 7f Standard and strong sim-going figures (12/15), partnered by 7lb claimer Miss Remie Morgan which helps on weight; the true hold-up style is squeezed toward midfield here, but if the pace is genuine this is one of the better-credentialled closers in the field.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, racing just 9 days after last start with course form figures of 4th and 6th at 6-7f Standard — Christopher Kellett sends this 7yo out in solid condition and with no rival to press him, the race is his to lose from the front.

runners_data.name: Beaming Light
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's 6yo carries hood/eye-shield, has 2 places from 11 sim-going runs but no wins on this surface; pushed forward by the hold-up crowd congestion and will likely race in a more prominent spot than its natural style dictates, meaning it is neither fish nor fowl tactically.

runners_data.name: Cooramook
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claim) aboard this 4yo who has an excellent placed record at 7f Standard (6 places from 12 sim-going runs, zero wins), suggesting consistency without quite finding top gear; a genuine hold-up type who should get a clear rear-field position and is the most reliable place-hitter in the field.

runners_data.name: Iconic Times
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a big jockey booking for a Jennie Candlish 4yo who won at 7f Standard (1W3P sim-going), though a 59-day absence is a concern; a natural hold-up type who should find a genuine rearward berth, but needs Bowen to find daylight in a field with many late-movers.

runners_data.name: Velvet Skies
runners_data.note: W H Harrison's 5yo is 76 days fresh and lacks headgear despite trying it in the past; plod-form at 6-7f Standard (0W4P from 12 sim-going runs) marks it as a consistent but non-winning hold-up performer, and the lengthy absence adds risk.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: John Ryan's 4yo has useful placed form at shorter trips and on Good ground but the sim-going record (7/15, 1W2P) is only fair; a natural hold-up type displaced toward midfield, though the drop to 7f on Standard is a slight unknown given recent 8f runs on softer surfaces.

runners_data.name: African Spirit
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a notable jockey booking for Ian Williams, but the horse's sim-going record is modest (5/11, 1W2P) and the move from 8-10f Good ground to 7f Standard requires some adaptation; races in tongue-tie and a pull — a genuine hold-up horse displaced toward midfield who needs pace to develop late.

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 4yo has solid sim-going experience (13/15 runs on Standard) but only 1 place and no wins; returned from 70 days off, runs without headgear, and is a true hold-up type that the map places toward midfield — this looks a tough ask to make an impact.

runners_data.name: Based
runners_data.note: William Knight's 3yo has an excellent profile at 7f Standard (1W3P from 7/8 sim-going runs) and races just 9 days after a run, suggesting freshness is managed; Taylor Fisher takes the ride, and though a natural hold-up horse, the consistent placed record at this exact trip and surface makes it one of the most reliable hold-up contenders in the race.

runners_data.name: Havanita
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings' 4yo wears a visor, is flagged as fading in finishes, and the sim-going record is a concern (3/8, 0W0P on Standard); a natural closer displaced toward midfield and tagged with a finishing fade flag — this is the lowest-probability hold-up runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: White Umbrella is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 7f Wolverhampton handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset — a genuinely sustainable gallop on standard Polytrack that will not burn off hold-up horses but equally will not hand them a sprint-finish on a plate. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types: Dashing Donkey, Faster Bee, Emery Down, African Spirit, Megaphone, Beaming Light and Havanita are all true closers pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; Cooramook, Iconic Times and Based are the hold-up runners most likely to occupy the genuinely rearward berths. With White Umbrella controlling tempo unopposed and the pace moderate, prominent-to-midfield racers who can travel within striking range will be best placed, while true hold-up horses shuffled even further back by the congested rear-end will find the closing sectionals insufficient to reel in a well-rated front-runner dictating terms. This race shape favours horses that can race in the first half of the field, travel economically behind the sole pace-setter and produce a sustained drive from two furlongs out rather than a sharp late sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: White Umbrella Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If White Umbrella bowls along uncontested and sets a pace comfortable enough to sustain, turning for home with a length or two in hand.
scenarios.body: White Umbrella, a confirmed front-runner fresh off a 9-day turnaround and with proven course form, dictates every yard and the moderate gallop means no rival can muster enough pace from the rear to close the gap; horses that have tracked prominently without over-committing are the only realistic challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse in the first four races fluidly off White Umbrella's heels and produces a clean, sustained challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Based (1W3P at 7f on Standard, apprentice-claimed weight) or Cooramook (consistent placed record at this trip and course) loom as the logical trackers who can sit just off the pace, conserve energy through the race and then pick up White Umbrella when the front-runner ties up in the closing stages; this shape rewards horses with tactical versatility and a reliable finishing kick rather than a deep closing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected or White Umbrella over-extends early, creating a meaningful gap in the closing sectionals for late challengers.
scenarios.body: Faster Bee (course-specialist, 2W at 7f Standard, strong late form) or Iconic Times (1W at Wolverhampton Standard) could benefit if the field concertinas into the turn and opens ground on the outside; however, the redistribution of so many genuine closers to midfield mapping makes this a congested, low-percentage scenario and the winner would need a clean passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Field Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If White Umbrella goes too fast for the conditions or compounds sharply inside the final two furlongs, triggering a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: An unlikely shape given the lone pace scenario, but if the front-runner over-races early any prominent holder such as Emery Down or Beaming Light could swoop; the glut of hold-up horses all making ground simultaneously would produce a messy finish and the winner would be whichever late-closer finds the cleanest run.

watchPoints.text: White Umbrella (William Carver) shows on track alone in front — watch whether any runner jumps sharply and attempts to press or match strides early, as any unexpected challenger could transform the pace and unsettle the race shape entirely.

Based and Cooramook are the hold-up types with the best recent placed form at 7f Standard — watch their draw positions at the off; if they secure inside-rail berths they can travel economically and pose a material threat to the leader late.

Faster Bee (Miss Remie Morgan, 7lb claim) has a strong course record but must overcome the rear-field congestion — watch whether the jockey commits to a wide outside run or hunts a gap through the pack, as track position in the straight will define her chance.

Havanita is flagged as a horse that fades in finishes — if it is prominent in running in the final furlong and then declines, it could cause interference with other closers making late runs, particularly in a field where several horses converge simultaneously.

Iconic Times (Sean Bowen, 59 days off) and Velvet Skies (76 days off) are both returning from extended absences — watch for any signs of race-rustiness or lack of fitness in the closing stages, which would confirm the race is effectively between the freshest horses.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with solid Standard-going form (1W5P in similar conditions) and six days since last run; the tongue-tie is retained, Christian Howarth claims 3lb, and five placings in fifteen similar starts underlines a steady if not explosive profile — danger if Reputation softens the pace perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but not dominant, On Key has finished in the top three in all six of his last six starts, with a win two starts back; he has experience of today's trip and going, yet 137 lb is a stern ask and he remains hard to win with.

runners_data.name: Captain Pickles
runners_data.note: Three wins and seven places from twelve Standard-going starts is a formidable record and Tony Culhane's yard is live (1/6 T14); ran off the front end over 7-8f on Standard and arrives 26 days fresh — a hold-up tag is absent, making this one of the cleaner prominent profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Musical Soldier
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claim) partners a horse whose last two runs produced a win and a second over 7f on Standard, making the form rock-solid; in truth a genuine hold-up type, but the crowded rear means he will race more prominently than he would like, and that positional compromise must be weighed against a trainer in hot form (6/23 T14).
runners_data.comment: Musical Soldier arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and placed in three of his five most recent starts, with experience of today's trip and going; a trainer firing at 28% seals his claims, though carrying 135 lb is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Mythical Isle
runners_data.note: Has one win from thirteen Standard-going starts and arrives 24 days since a 7th-of-9 last time, which is hardly inspiring; Patrick Morris is 0/8 in the 14-day window and this is a natural closer who will be shuffled forward by the congested field — the style compromise stacks on top of moderate recent form.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out makes Mythical Isle hard to fancy despite a win two starts back, and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures he faces a stiff ask; has run over today's trip and going before, at least, and 24 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: South Kensington
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on a 59-day fresh horse who has won twice and placed three times from eleven Standard starts at this trip; a genuine hold-up operator who needs the race to develop a real gallop, and with Reputation likely to go easy, this runner faces a structural disadvantage — strong overall profile but tactically awkward today.
runners_data.comment: South Kensington won two starts back and was second three starts back, but a fifth last time out after 59 days off gives pause; she has experience of today's trip and going, yet her official mark of 59 suggests she'll need to find improvement to dominate from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with only one placing from fifteen Standard-going starts (0W1P), whose recent form reads 9-8-6-9-5 — the experience is not masking a performance absence, and Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim cannot paper over a profile that struggles badly on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Redredrobin has run over today's trip and going before, and her rating of 67 — ranking her highest of the 12 — makes her a genuine threat at the weights carrying 140 lb from stall 11; the concern is she's winless in her last five starts, with recent finishes failing to suggest a breakthrough is imminent.

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners a horse fitted with a visor, returning 16 days after a second over 7f on Standard — the only win in recent history came in identical conditions, so the trip and surface are right; however, as a hold-up type reliant on a strong pace, today's likely moderate gallop set by Reputation is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Midnight's Dream has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the worry is that he's been winless in his last six starts, and 139 lb from stall 10 may test his resolution.

runners_data.name: Reputation
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner ridden by James Sullivan for Ruth Carr, who holds 2W4P from thirteen Standard starts, and won last time out over this exact course and distance 25 days ago — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a mild caution that the prominent tag is a slight stretch, but the ability to dictate entirely is the key tactical weapon here.
runners_data.comment: Reputation has won in his last five starts but the ninth last time out is impossible to ignore, and ranked ninth of 12 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here. Has run over today's trip and going, and 25 days between runs suggests he's fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: Laura Pearson takes the ride on David Loughnane's three-year-old, who wears a hood and has no recorded Standard-going form in the history provided — all five career starts came on Good, and without going comparables this runner carries meaningful uncertainty; a hold-up type needing a strong pace she is unlikely to get.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yoko does have a second two starts back to offer as encouragement, and she has run over today's trip before; carrying 134 lb from stall six, she faces a stiff task against eleven rivals on a 20-day break.

runners_data.name: The Spotlight Kid
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin partners Dean Ivory's seven-year-old, who wears blinkers and is 72 days absent — that lay-off is the headline concern; 1W6P from fourteen Standard starts is a perfectly respectable record and the prominent style fits today's shape, but freshness after over two months off must be factored in.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, The Spotlight Kid faces a stiff ask here; 72 days off is a concern, though he has distance and going experience, and draw one from 133 lb at least gives him a clean early position.

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: Richard Phillips is 0/3 in the 14-day window and this horse steps back from 8f to 7f, where it has no wins from fifteen Standard starts; a genuine closer by nature, it will find itself racing out of its comfort zone with the field compressing the rear — the p headgear retains, and three places at 8f on Standard suggest it stays better than it sprints.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Manton Road faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a placed effort last time out offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Oh So Perfect
runners_data.note: Alistair Rawlinson rides Michael Appleby's three-year-old, who has won twice and placed five times from nine Standard starts — 2W5P is a standout record in this company; three consecutive placed efforts including two wins over 7f on Standard on the last three starts makes this prominent racer the most in-form horse in the field, and the low weight (130lbs) adds appeal.
runners_data.comment: Oh So Perfect arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, and second last time out keeps her firmly in the mix; she has run over today's trip and going before, and nine days since her last start suggests she is fresh and ready. The cold trainer form is the one note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Reputation is the confirmed front-runner and, with only On Key, Captain Pickles, The Spotlight Kid, and Oh So Perfect as genuine prominent types, the pace should be controlled and sustainable rather than frantic — Reputation can dictate from the front without being seriously pressured for supremacy. The field is back-heavy with hold-up horses, but Musical Soldier, Mythical Isle, and Manton Road are all true hold-up types who cannot get their natural position in this race shape and will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, artificially compressing the midfield. With Reputation likely to roll along at a steady, uncontested clip on Standard Polytrack, the race sets up as a test of which prominent or tracking horse picks up most efficiently in the straight. This pace shape clearly favours prominent racers who can travel just off the leader and pounce inside the final furlong — hold-up horses face a genuinely compromised task given the lack of a truly strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Reputation Leads, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Reputation dictates a controlled, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers travel smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Reputation sets a sustainable tempo that strings the field out neatly, and the horses sitting second or third in the box seat get first run from the two-furlong pole without having to find a gap. Prominent racers with strong Standard-going form — particularly those settled just off the leader — are ideally placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge Denied
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the prominent horses kick early, burning off the closers before they can respond.
scenarios.body: Reputation goes so easy that the front rank effectively gets a free rail to quicken from well out, meaning no room is left for hold-up horses to run through. Horses like South Kensington and Midnight's Dream, who need a true gallop, find the race over before they can get organised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and the closers find a clear passage to run through.
scenarios.body: South Kensington or Midnight's Dream, if the race develops any semblance of a genuine gallop in the middle portion, could storm home from off the pace — South Kensington's two wins at seven furlongs on Standard make this the most credible hold-up threat. However, the redistributed horses artificially crowding midfield reduce clean-passage probability materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Reputation is never seriously challenged and the field fails to mount a coherent challenge, leaving the leader to simply coast home.
scenarios.body: With only one confirmed front-runner and a field of horses either out of position or struggling for form, Reputation could exploit the tactical vacuum and simply steal the race from start to finish. Ruth Carr's record of 2W4P on Standard going in similar scenarios gives this low-probability shape marginal credence.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Perfect has recorded 2W5P from nine Standard starts and arrives in the best recent form in the race — if it secures a prominent pitch just off Reputation, it is the single most dangerous winner profile in the field.

Reputation's controlled front-running is the key pace variable — if James Sullivan crosses unchallenged and sets a truly dawdling gallop, hold-up horses including South Kensington and Midnight's Dream will find the race tactically ruined before the turn.

Musical Soldier, Mythical Isle, and Manton Road are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield by the race shape — watch whether any of them drift back to their natural position at the start, as that would further thin out the prominent pack and alter how much cover Reputation gets.

The Spotlight Kid is 72 days absent for Dean Ivory, a trainer whose recent strike rate is modest (1/3 T14) — a first-time blinkers or fitness query run is possible, and its prominent style could see it go hard early before fading late if short of peak fitness.

Redredrobin's Standard-going record of 0W1P from fifteen starts is a striking surface aversion — Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim reduces the weight burden but cannot address a fundamental incompatibility with Polytrack conditions that persists across the horse's entire recent history.
